correctness.rationale: Gaussian normalization and finite monomial tilt preserve independent standard distant coordinates. Their centered normalized squared moduli are an orthonormal sequence in weighted L²; Bessel inequality proves tail-insertion vanishing for each bounded Toeplitz symbol. The diagonal C*-closure preserves the limit. Compactness forces eigenvalues along distant orthonormal sectors to vanish, hence all coefficients vanish; comparing a sector with its distant insertion gives the exact 1/2 distance, attained by I/2. Finite-prefix singleton projections lie in finite-dimensional square-root-metric Toeplitz algebras, proving strict inclusion.

originality.rationale: The motivating full-text 2022 article explicitly poses projection nonmembership and equality of (5.9) as unresolved. The new Bessel tail-insertion condition is an algebra-closed invariant, unlike their Example 5.9 single-generator obstruction. It yields nonmembership, exact 1/2 distance, no nonzero compact elements, and strictness of the requested inclusion for all finite block sizes. Published finite-dimensional Fock and infinite Hardy analogues do not imply these statements in the specified Gaussian infinite-variable model. Originality remains historically qualified by inaccessible 1995 full text and possible unindexed stronger results.
residual_risks: The author-uploaded Janas–Rudol 1995 full-text PDF was unavailable, so a stronger general C*-algebra statement in that source cannot be excluded by complete examination.

The full Guo–Yan 2022 Hardy-polydisc text and full original Dewage–Ólafsson 2022 article were not directly read; their verified abstracts and the latter theorem as restated in Bauer–Rodriguez Rodriguez were used.
Search results may miss later unindexed or differently named equivalent work; the checked 2022 explicit open problem is positive evidence, not independent confirmation of historical uniqueness.
